first_aid: Wash the affected area gently with a mild cleanser and lukewarm water.
Apply over-the-counter treatments containing benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid.
Avoid popping, squeezing, or picking at the pimples to prevent scarring and infection.
Acne and Rosacea Photos.warning: If the condition is painful, cystic, or does not improve with over-the-counter treatments, consult a dermatologist.

first_aid: Do not attempt to treat, scratch, or remove the lesion at home.
Keep the area clean and dry.
Protect the affected area from sun exposure by wearing protective clothing and sunscreen.
Actinic Keratosis Basal Cell Carcinoma a.warning: These are potentially cancerous or precancerous lesions. Seek immediate evaluation from a dermatologist for a biopsy and proper medical treatment.

first_aid: Apply a thick layer of fragrance-free moisturizer or emollient immediately after bathing.
Take short, lukewarm baths or showers instead of hot ones.
Use mild, unscented soap and avoid harsh scrubbing.
Atopic Dermatitis Photos.warning: If the skin becomes infected (oozing pus, yellow crusts) or if itching prevents sleep, seek medical attention.

first_aid: There is no home first aid for suspected skin cancer. Do not apply any home remedies.
Keep the lesion clean and avoid picking at it if it bleeds or crusts over.
Cover with a sterile bandage if it is actively bleeding.
Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC).warning: BCC is a type of skin cancer. You must schedule an appointment with a dermatologist for diagnosis and surgical removal.

first_aid: These are generally harmless growths. Leave them alone.
Do not try to scratch, pick, or freeze them off at home.
If they become irritated by clothing, cover them loosely with a bandage.
Benign Keratosis-like Lesions (BKL).warning: If the lesion changes in size, color, shape, or starts bleeding spontaneously, have it checked by a doctor to rule out malignancy.

first_aid: Do not pop or puncture the blisters, as the intact skin protects against infection.
Cover the area loosely with a sterile, non-stick dressing.
Keep the skin clean and avoid tight clothing that might rub the blisters.
Bullous Disease Photos.warning: Autoimmune blistering diseases require prescription medications (like systemic corticosteroids). See a doctor immediately.

first_aid: Wash the area gently with soap and water.
Apply a warm, moist compress to the affected area for 15-20 minutes to relieve pain.
Cover any open or oozing sores with a sterile bandage to prevent spreading.
Cellulitis Impetigo and other Bacterial.warning: Bacterial infections can spread rapidly to the bloodstream. If you experience fever, chills, or rapidly spreading redness, go to the emergency room.

first_aid: Moisturize the skin multiple times a day with thick creams or ointments.
Apply over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream (1%) to itchy areas for a few days.
Avoid known triggers such as extreme temperatures, harsh soaps, or rough fabrics.
Eczema Photos.warning: Consult a doctor if over-the-counter treatments fail or if signs of bacterial infection appear.

first_aid: Stop taking any newly introduced over-the-counter medications or supplements immediately.
Take cool showers and apply calamine lotion to soothe the rash.
Take an over-the-counter oral antihistamine to reduce itching.
Exanthems and Drug Eruptions.warning: If the rash is accompanied by fever, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face/tongue, or blisters on mucous membranes, seek emergency medical care immediately.

first_aid: Handle hair gently. Avoid tight hairstyles, harsh chemical treatments, and excessive heat styling.
Maintain a balanced diet rich in iron, protein, and vitamins.
Use a mild shampoo and avoid rubbing the scalp vigorously.
Hair Loss Photos Alopecia and other Hair.warning: Sudden or patchy hair loss can indicate an underlying medical condition. Consult a doctor for a proper diagnosis.

first_aid: Keep the affected area clean and dry to speed up healing.
Avoid sexual contact while sores or warts are present to prevent transmission.
Wash your hands thoroughly after touching the affected area.
Herpes HPV and other STDs Photos.warning: These are contagious viral infections. You must see a healthcare provider for antiviral prescriptions or clinical removal of warts.

first_aid: Strict sun protection is crucial. Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30+) daily.
Wear wide-brimmed hats and protective clothing when outdoors.
Avoid direct sun exposure during peak hours (10 AM to 4 PM).
Light Diseases and Disorders of Pigmenta.warning: While usually cosmetic, new or rapidly changing pigmented spots should be evaluated by a dermatologist to rule out melanoma.

first_aid: Avoid sun exposure completely, as UV light can trigger severe flare-ups.
Apply high-SPF, broad-spectrum sunscreen even when indoors near windows.
Rest and avoid physical exhaustion during a flare-up.
Lupus and other Connective Tissue diseas.warning: Systemic connective tissue diseases can affect internal organs. This requires ongoing management by a rheumatologist and dermatologist.

first_aid: Do not try to remove, scratch, or treat suspicious moles at home.
Take a clear photograph of the mole next to a ruler to track any changes.
Keep the area protected from the sun.
Melanoma Skin Cancer Nevi and Moles.warning: Melanoma is the deadliest form of skin cancer. Immediate dermatological evaluation, biopsy, and surgical excision are mandatory.

first_aid: Keep nails trimmed short and file down thick areas.
Wash and thoroughly dry your feet/hands, especially between the toes/fingers.
Avoid sharing nail clippers and wear breathable footwear.
Nail Fungus and other Nail Disease.warning: Fungal nail infections are notoriously stubborn. Over-the-counter treatments often fail; prescription oral or topical antifungals from a doctor are usually needed.

first_aid: Immediately wash the skin with lukewarm water and soap to remove plant oils or irritants.
Wash all clothes, shoes, and pets that may have come into contact with the allergen.
Apply calamine lotion or over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream to reduce itching.
Poison Ivy Photos and other Contact Derm.warning: If the rash covers a large portion of the body, affects the face/genitals, or causes severe swelling, seek medical attention for prescription steroids.

first_aid: Apply thick, heavy moisturizers daily to help soften plaques and reduce scaling.
Take daily baths with added colloidal oatmeal or Epsom salts to soothe the skin.
Avoid picking at scales, as this can trigger worsened flare-ups (Koebner phenomenon).
Psoriasis pictures Lichen Planus and rel.warning: These are chronic autoimmune conditions. A dermatologist can prescribe targeted topical treatments, phototherapy, or systemic biologics.

first_aid: For tick bites (Lyme risk): Carefully remove the tick with fine-tipped tweezers by grasping it close to the skin and pulling straight up.
Wash the bite area with rubbing alcohol or soap and water.
For scabies: Wash all bedding, clothing, and towels in hot water and dry on high heat.
Scabies Lyme Disease and other Infestati.warning: If you develop a 'bullseye' rash after a tick bite, or have widespread severe itching (scabies), you need prescription antibiotics or scabicides from a doctor.

first_aid: These 'barnacles of aging' are harmless. Do not attempt to pick or scrape them off.
If they itch, apply a mild over-the-counter moisturizer.
If clothing rubs against them, cover loosely with a bandage.
Seborrheic Keratoses and other Benign Tu.warning: If a lesion grows rapidly, bleeds, or turns black, it should be examined by a doctor to ensure it is not a melanoma masquerading as a benign tumor.

first_aid: Skin manifestations of systemic diseases (like diabetes, liver disease, or thyroid issues) cannot be treated with local first aid alone.
Maintain good general skin hygiene and moisturize dry areas.
Do not apply harsh chemicals or home remedies to the skin lesions.
Systemic Disease.warning: The skin rash is merely a symptom of an internal problem. Urgent evaluation by an internal medicine specialist is required.

first_aid: Apply an over-the-counter antifungal cream (like clotrimazole or terbinafine) twice daily.
Keep the affected area clean, dry, and exposed to air when possible.
Wash towels and clothing in hot water and do not share personal items.
Tinea Ringworm Candidiasis and other Fun.warning: If the infection does not improve after 2 weeks of OTC treatment, or if it affects the scalp or beard area, prescription oral antifungals are required.

first_aid: Take an over-the-counter non-drowsy antihistamine (like cetirizine or loratadine).
Apply cool compresses to the itchy areas to soothe the skin.
Avoid tight clothing, hot showers, and known allergic triggers.
Urticaria Hives.warning: DANGER: If hives are accompanied by swelling of the lips/tongue, difficulty breathing, or dizziness, this is anaphylaxis. Call emergency services immediately.

first_aid: Protect the area from trauma, as vascular tumors (like hemangiomas) can bleed heavily if scratched or cut.
If bleeding occurs, apply firm, continuous pressure with a clean cloth for 10-15 minutes.
Do not attempt any home removal techniques.
Vascular Tumors.warning: If bleeding cannot be stopped with pressure, go to the emergency room. Consult a doctor for cosmetic or medical treatment options.

first_aid: Elevate the affected limbs (usually the legs) to reduce swelling and pressure.
Keep the skin clean and avoid any tight clothing or elastic bands that restrict blood flow.
Rest and avoid prolonged standing.
Vasculitis Photos.warning: Vasculitis is an inflammation of the blood vessels and can affect internal organs. Immediate medical evaluation by a rheumatologist or dermatologist is necessary.

first_aid: Cover the wart or molluscum bumps with a bandage to prevent spreading the virus to others or other parts of your body.
Do not pick, scratch, or shave over the areas.
For common warts, you can try over-the-counter salicylic acid patches as directed.
Warts Molluscum and other Viral Infectio.warning: If the warts are painful, spreading rapidly, or located on the face/genitals, do not use OTC treatments. See a doctor for cryotherapy or prescription creams.
